business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (bijural): Civil Law for Quebec private and commercial law; Common Law for federal public law, criminal law and tax procedure; Charter of the French Language applies to commercial naming and registration documents.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1980), as amended
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Registration Regulations, SOR/2007-121. Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236 and following; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: UBO information is collected in the Quebec enterprise registry and accessible to authorized enforcement, tax and anti-money-laundering authorities; it is not a generally searchable public UBO register. The limited partnership agreement and internal partnership register remain private.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status of every corporate general partner and corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar in the partner's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization through Global Affairs Canada or the Embassy/Consulate concerned

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and board / member resolutions authorizing execution of the Quebec limited partnership contract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, board of directors or equivalent governing body of the corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where the Quebec registrar or financial institution requires it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport / national identity card of every signing individual, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office or issuing civil authority; copy certified by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a notary, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the recipient authority so requires

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and evidence of source of funds for capital contribution to the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized or legalized as required by the receiving Quebec notary or financial intermediary; apostille may be requested for foreign bank documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Quebec resident representative / registered agent for service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the origin jurisdiction or the appointing partner's authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if origin is a Hague Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership register extract / UBO chain breakdown for each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate general partner's legal representative or registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified as true and complete by counsel; apostille or consular legalization is required when the document will be filed into the Quebec civil registry or relied upon by a Quebec notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every partner, nominee, authorized signatory, director and 25% or greater ultimate beneficial owner against OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated List, Public Safety Canada sanctions lists, and other applicable terrorism financing lists. PEP status must be determined using a risk-based approach with enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, including source of funds and source of wealth verification for contributions above CAD 50,000. Ongoing negative news monitoring and transaction monitoring are required for the vintage luxury resale industry due to the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec / Registre des entreprises du Quebec online portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Quebec societe en commandite must comply with the Charter of the French Language. It must be filed in French, and any non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters. English words are permitted only where no French equivalent exists or where the enterprise qualifies for an exception such as a recognized trademark. The name must include the phrase 'societe en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.' in appropriate legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file written representations to the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the rejection decision. If the Registraire upholds the rejection, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Superior Court of Quebec pursuant to the Code of Civil Procedure. A revised name can be submitted immediately without affecting the appeal of the original name. Extensions of the initial reservation may be requested only where the underlying registration is actively delayed by a competent authority and the request is made before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for an online-only resale business only if it constitutes a genuine service address operated by a licensed registered agent or law firm that receives legal process and administrative mail in Quebec. It cannot be a non-address post-office box. The registered office address must correspond to the principal establishment disclosed to the Registraire des entreprises and must be available for service of process. Tax registration with Revenu Quebec and GST/QST authorities requires a physical or verifiable address for audit correspondence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 25% probability of an unannounced physical compliance inspection within the first 36 months for a purely online vintage luxury resale entity. The probability rises to approximately 65% if annual transaction volume exceeds CAD 2 million, if GST/QST audit triggers arise, or if sanctions/PEP screening flags are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2246 and 2251-2264 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 18-38 and 76-82 (registration, declarations, beneficial ownership); Regulation respecting the register of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1; referred complementary: Act respecting the Régie de l'assurance-dépôt du Québec (inapplicable to non-securities LPs) and the Québec Companies Act for a corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Direction de l'immatriculation, Québec City
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed electronically through the REQ secure portal under P-44.1, s. 18; accompanied by the initial declaration of establishment and, where the general partner is a corporation, its articles and attestation of existence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital. Each limited partner must make the contribution recited in the partnership agreement (cash or property); limited liability is conditioned upon the contribution being actually made and recorded in the capital accounts (CCQ art. 2242). No escrow account is mandated at registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Board adopts the limited partnership agreement of the proposed LP and approves the admission of the initial general and limited partners, together with the contribution schedules recorded in the capital accounts ledger; (2) The registered office of the limited partnership is established at [Québec address] and the general partner is directed to file the declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (3) [Name] is appointed Chief Compliance Officer and [Name] Operations Manager, each authorized to execute filings and payment agreements; (4) Banking, Stripe, and escrow accounts are authorized; (5) Registration, permit, and tax fees are approved. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation request through the REQ portal (or the authorized NUANS channel) submitting at least three French-language name proposals ending with 'S.E.C.', 'société en commandite' or 'L.P.'. The proposed name must be distinctive, not misleading, and respect the Éditeur officiel du Québec drafting rules. Upon approval, the reservation certificate is issued and remains valid for 120 days.
required_dossiers: Three proposed names for the limited partnership
Identification of the general partner (name, jurisdiction, corporate number if applicable)
Signed authorization of the general partner for the name application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused (confusion or prohibited term), file an amended proposal within the response window, or request a review with the REQ Director under P-44.1, s. 22; alternatively, select a new distinct name and re-submit the reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of partnership agreement and recording of capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private deed executed among partners (no government filing at this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the French-language limited partnership agreement in writing (notarial deed recommended but not mandatory). The agreement must identify the general partner with unlimited liability and each limited partner, define the contribution obligations and profit-sharing ratio, and contain management provisions. Execute the certificate of contribution and open the capital accounts ledger.
required_dossiers: Duly signed limited partnership agreement
Sworn statement or bank confirmation evidencing each partner's capital contribution
Consent of the general partner to act in that capacity
Copy of the general partner's certificate of existence if corporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend and re-serve the agreement by a supplementary deed if a partner fails to execute; latent defects are cured by unanimous resolution evidenced in writing; contributions may be re-designated in kind with an independent valuation report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the limited partnership with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online filing via Mon espace d'affaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ portal, complete the initial declaration of registration (déclaration d'immatriculation) for the limited partnership, indicating the enterprise's name, establishment address in Québec, general partner identity, activities (NAICS 459510), and place of business. Pay the registration fee. Upon acceptance, REQ issues the enterprise number (NEQ) and the certificate of registration serving as conclusive evidence of existence under P-44.1, s. 27.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic declaration of registration
Lease or proof of address for the registered office and principal establishment
Name reservation certificate
Identification of the general partner and, where corporate, its articles and Québec registration
Contact information of a natural person responsible for the registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues an avis de défaut or a refusal, cure by correcting the declared data and paying the applicable fee within the indicated delay; a skipped declaration may be re-filed online; systemic refusal triggers the review mechanism under P-44.1, ss. 19 and 42.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and provincial tax registrations (BN, GST/HST, QST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (tax and QST) and Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST and payroll) — accès RM / CRA Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, register through Revenu Québec's online service for a federal Business Number (BN), GST/HST account (mandatory once taxable worldwide supplies exceed CAD 30,000) and Québec Sales Tax (QST) account. Register the payroll source-deductions account if employees are hired. Elections for the LP: file the partnership information return (TP-600) and T5013 information slips in subsequent fiscal years.
required_dossiers: Enterprise number (NEQ) and certificate of registration
Partnership agreement and list of partners with SIN/QSSN for resident individuals
Projected annual taxable supplies declaration
Banking coordinates for Government of Canada/Revenu Québec direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late or incomplete registrations are correctable by filing amended forms online; interest and penalties are generally waived if voluntary disclosure and payment occur before the CRA/Revenu Québec initiates a compliance action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial ownership declaration and municipal permits acquisition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) and Ville de Montréal — Service des permis et inspections
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File with REQ the mandatory declaration of beneficial ownership (déclaration de bénéficiaire ultime), stating every individual who, directly or indirectly, holds 25% or more of the partnership or controls it, and keep the register current within 30 days of any change. Concurrently, submit to Ville de Montréal the municipal business license application (permis d'exploitation d'entreprise) for a second-hand goods retail establishment, attaching the fire safety certificate and the lease.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership register entries (name, address, date of birth, control basis)
Municipal business permit application form
Fire safety certificate for the claimed premises
Proof of occupation (lease) and civil liability insurance certificate
Letter attesting the consignment sales model and non-pawn operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: REQ penalty for late beneficial ownership filing is cured by immediate submission with a voluntary disclosure letter. Municipal permit refusal may be appealed under the Ville de Montréal permitting regulation; deficiencies are remedied by submitting amended plans or additional fire-prevention documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ville de Montréal — Service des permis et inspections (permis d'exploitation d'entreprise, arts. 20-78 RVQ) and, at the provincial level, the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for workplaces
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'exploitation d'entreprise — commerce de vente d'articles de seconde main (municipal business license for the retail of second-hand goods, including online consignment), together with a registre de police (transaction ledger) for traceability of consigned luxury items

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction régionale de l'analyse et de l'expertise régionales, Montréal
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — full EIA review not triggered (dry goods warehousing and e-commerce retail without industrial processing); subject to municipal stormwater and waste bylaws
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge limited to sanitary uses; compliance with the Règlement sur le rejet des eaux usées dans les réseaux d'égout (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 28.2) and Ville de Montréal sewer bylaws (no process wastewater). VOC emissions: negligible; storage areas must respect the Règlement sur les halocarbures and fire code ventilation limits. Waste: handling of scraps, damaged leather goods and packaging under the Loi sur la qualité de l'environnement (CQLR c. Q-2) and the Règlement sur l'enfouissement et l'incinération de matières résiduelles; no hazardous waste generation other than incidental e-waste directed to certified recoverers (REP program under OCPMR).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: certificate of conformity issued by the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal and compliance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code for the storage area; structure: engineering verification of floor loading for shelving and vaults under the Quebec Construction Code (c. B-1.1, r. 3) if pallet racking exceeds 2.4 m; workplace: CNESST registration and prevention program, occupational health and safety plan, and accessibility clearance for the public entrance under the Act to secure handicapped persons in the exercise of their rights.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal Business Registration Online (BRO) portal for Business Number (BN) issuance; Revenu Québec (RQ) — 'clics affaires' portal and the Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) and QST account administration. RQ administers both the federal GST (TPS) and the provincial QST under a collection and harmonization agreement with the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine small supplier status — an LP whose total worldwide taxable supplies are $30,000 CAD or less per calendar quarter and per previous four quarters is exempt from mandatory registration. Step 2: Non-resident LPs apply to CRA via Form RC3911 'GST/HST and QST Registration for Non-Resident Persons' or through BRO; CRA issues a BN with program account suffix 'RT' for the partnership as a distinct registrant 'person' under ETA s.272.1. Step 3: In Quebec, the LP must obtain an NEQ from REQ (required for any operating business), then register for QST by linking the QST account to the federal BN (suffix 'TQ'), through RQ's clics affaires. Step 4: If permanent establishment exists in Quebec, the LP must also file provincial income tax administrative records; non-resident partners without a PE file directly with CRA. Step 5: Use RQ's CLIC registration package to elect electronic returns and designate a representative in Quebec (mandatory for non-resident registrants).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — Under ITA s.96, the LP is fiscally transparent for income tax: no entity-level federal or Quebec income tax; each partner includes allocated profit/loss on a calendar-year or partnership fiscal-year basis. For GST/HST/QST, the LP is a deemed 'person' that is a separate registrant and must charge, collect, and remit tax on taxable supplies; partners do not jointly remit partnership GST. Quebec treats the LP identically for QST under the Quebec Taxation Act Art. 772 and the QST rules, preserving flow-through characterization and avoiding hybrid mismatch in the Canada-U.S./Canada-EU context.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' regime exists in Canada. Elections available: (a) partnership fiscal year end election under ITA s.249.1 to use a non-calendar year (subject to deferral rules); (b) s.216 election for non-resident partners to report rental income on a net basis; (c) GST/HST Quick Method election (ETA s.228.1) for eligible small suppliers, including vintage resellers, using simplified remittance on gross sales; (d) Streamlined Accounting and electronic filing election for non-resident digital service vendors (ETA s.180.1) effective July 1, 2021; (e) ETA s.273 joint election for closely related corporations/partnerships, applicable to the LP when a corporation is the general partner; (f) QST Input Tax Rebate election for resident partners in a selected financial partnership; (g) Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA s.18.4–18.6 apply automatically where a partner's residence jurisdiction treats the LP as opaque — no opt-out election is available; the LP must document partner country classifications to prevent disallowed deductions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.exemption_zone_status: No special tax-exempt zone applies to e-commerce in Quebec. Goods entering the Province of Quebec are not exempt municipal zone. Duty and import GST/QST may apply at customs for goods imported into Canada from a foreign source.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.de_minimis_and_foreign_entity_limits: Registration is permissive until the $30,000 CAD threshold; after threshold, GST/HST and QST registration is mandatory, assessed per calendar quarter on worldwide taxable supplies. No minimum capital, no Canadian citizenship requirement, and foreign partners may own 100% of the LP; however, non-resident partners must obtain a CRA individual or corporate tax account to report Canadian allocated income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) integrated with Quebec Sales Tax (QST) — administered jointly by Revenu Québec; the GST portion is the 5% federal tax, the QST is a 9.975% provincial VAT under the Quebec Sales Tax Act; combined effective rate 14.975% on the consideration excluding QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: 30,000 CAD small supplier threshold (per single calendar quarter and previous four consecutive quarters), measured on worldwide taxable supplies; QST: also 30,000 CAD measured on worldwide taxable supplies, with the same quarterly test. For non-resident digital platform vendors of intangible and services to Canadian consumers (as 'specified supplies'), the simplified registration regime requires registration once Canadian consumer sales exceed 30,000 CAD, with an annual return and simplified rate tables; this threshold is also applied to online consignment and secondhand luxury resale platforms operating into Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory government-issued digital clearance, API stamping, or real-time fiscal control regime. The CRA and RQ operate a voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing infrastructure using the PEPPOL network; adoption is optional but encouraged for large retailers. RQ mandates that all invoices issued in Quebec be drawn up in French (Charter of the French Language), and must contain: the legal full name of the LP, the trading name if different, the BN and GST/HST/QST account numbers, date, description of the supply, the amount of consideration, and the tax amount charged (or a clear statement that the supply is zero-rated or exempt). For QST purposes, the invoice must state 'TPS 5% / TVQ 9.975%' on separate lines; where a customer is non-resident and the supply is zero-rated, the invoice must state '0% TPS / 0% TVQ' with the export documentation cross-referenced.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.place_of_supply_and_nexus_note: For vintage luxury goods resold online: tangible personal property is taxed at the place of delivery/possession (ETA s.142.1 and Quebec place-of-supply rules). Supplies made in Quebec attract 5% GST and 9.975% QST; goods delivered outside Quebec attract only GST (or provincial HST if delivered to a participating province). Services such as authentication, insurance, and escrow are taxed based on the recipient's province of residence. When the LP sells to a non-resident buyer and the goods are sent from Quebec to an address outside Canada, the supply is zero-rated (0% GST and 0% QST), provided the LP obtains export evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI Part V s.1–5 when the LP exports the vintage luxury goods from Canada, the goods are delivered to a non-resident consignee outside Canada, and the export is documented (proof of removal from Canada within 60 days after delivery to the carrier). Services exports: zero-rated under s.7 when (i) the service is supplied to a non-resident person, (ii) the service is not performed in Canada for a Canadian resident, and (iii) the client is not in Canada at the time the service is performed; for consignment services (listing, authentication, escrow and resale of luxury goods on behalf of foreign sellers) these criteria are met if the foreign seller/consignor is a non-resident. For a non-resident consignor, the LP may act as a commissionaire and charge its commission; the commission is zero-rated when made to the non-resident principal. Retrospective application: the zero-rated export status must be claimed at the time of the sale with cumulative documentation; failure to keep export evidence within 6 months of filing means the supply is re-characterized as taxable in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial Invoice — full legal name of LP, buyer, unit price, quantity, HS tariff code for each luxury item (e.g., HS 42.02, 71.13, 91.01), and declaration 'Exported from Canada for consumption outside Canada'.

Customs Export Declaration — Canada Customs Coding Form B13A (paper) or Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) / Electronic Export Reporting via the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), filed for shipments above the $2,000 or $2,500 exemption threshold; date and reference number must match invoice.

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill — through carrier bill showing the LP as exporter/consignor, the foreign buyer as consignee, and a clearly designated Canadian port of loading and foreign port of discharge.

Inward Remittance Certificate / Payment Evidence — SWIFT MT103, Escrow.com settlement, or Payment processor deposit record, demonstrating the funds received in the LP's Canadian or foreign bank account from the non-resident buyer; note that the $30,000 CAD small supplier threshold applies to turnover, and repatriation of proceeds is mandatory within the fiscal year.
Packing List — showing carton marks, weights, serial numbers for luxury watches/handbags, and destination address.
For exported services: signed service agreement, purchase order, and invoice with delivery address outside Canada and a statement of the non-resident recipient's role (universal no-placement rules).
Carrier's proof of removal: leaving certificate or final delivery receipt signed by the foreign buyer or customs clearing broker abroad.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and RQ jointly audit export zero-rating claims under ETA s.296; normal reassessment period is 4 years from the filing date, extended indefinitely to 7 years where misrepresentation or negligence is shown. If the documentary bundle is incomplete or the 60-day export rule is breached, the zero-rating is invalidated: the LP is assessed output GST/HST and QST at the standard rate (14.975%) on the full sales price, plus compound daily interest (s.280). Penalties: gross negligence under s.285.1 is 50% of the amount of tax that was sought to be avoided or incorrectly refunded; evasion under s.327 (willful fraud) carries a fine of not less than 50% and up to 200% of the tax evaded, plus imprisonment of up to 5 years. In Quebec, RQ may also issue director/partner liability notices, revoke the LP's registration, and add a 25% administrative fine for false QST claims. Any refund obtained through fraudulent export zero-rating is clawed back with retroactive effect, and the exporter may be excluded from PEPPOL e-invoicing and export tariff benefits. For consignment resale, if the LP claims zero-rating on goods that are not actually exported (e.g., delivered to a warehouse in Quebec for later sale to a Canadian resident buyer), the full tax applies, and the LP is liable for penalties and foreign exchange translation losses based on the CRA monthly average exchange rate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority and the sole issuer of Canadian bank notes under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2). Canada has not maintained a separate foreign exchange control administration since the abolition of exchange controls on December 14, 1951. The Department of Finance Canada and Global Affairs Canada jointly administer cross-border financial sanctions and trade controls; FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) is the financial intelligence unit for anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing reporting, and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises federal Schedule I banks. The Quebec jurisdiction adds the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for securities and provincial financial-sector conduct, and Revenu Québec for provincial tax and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) compliance, although banking and FX are federally regulated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) enjoys full de jure and de facto convertibility on both the current account and the capital account, with no statutory requirement for Central Bank approval of cross-border remittances or capital transactions. Canada maintains an independent floating exchange rate regime; the Bank of Canada does not intervene in foreign exchange markets and no quantitative convertibility ceilings exist. For the Quebec Limited Partnership (CA_LP), profit and capital distributions to non-resident limited partners are freely remittable in CAD or USD. A non-resident partner of a Canadian partnership remains taxable in Canada on its share of Canadian-source business income under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Part IV of the Taxation Act (Quebec), except where a tax treaty limits Canadian taxing rights. Distributions representing return of contributed capital and, in most cases, allocated business income are not subject to Part XIII withholding; Part XIII withholding applies only to enumerated 'passive' payments (e.g., rents, royalties, management-fee income, and certain interest) sourced to Canada. Practical banking constraints are limited to institution-level documentary due diligence and FINTRAC reporting of electronic funds transfers (EFTs) of CAD 10,000 or more, not to any restriction on capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation on export proceeds or on any foreign currency earned by Canadian residents. A resident exporter, such as the CA_LP engaged in cross-border online consignment resale, may retain US dollars and other foreign currency indefinitely in bank accounts at Canadian banks or in foreign correspondent accounts. The only enforceable obligations are (i) FINTRAC reporting of all cross-border EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and associated regulations, which the reporting bank discharges, and (ii) the declaration to the Canada Border Services Agency of physical import/export of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or greater. No export documentation other than the standard commercial invoice, customs declaration, and shipping records is required for FX purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as an auxiliary payment rail; LOW as a primary treasury account. Offshore digital EMI providers (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, or any European-licensed e-money institution) may lawfully serve as collection/disbursement accelerators for the CA_LP, but they cannot replace a Canadian Schedule I bank account because the partnership must hold its corporate operating and escrow liquidity with a prudentially regulated and FINTRAC-reporting Canadian financial institution to support the commercial payment rails (Stripe and Escrow_Pay) and to preserve clean audit trails. Legal constraints include: (i) any EMI processing CAD or holding accounts for a Canadian resident entity must be registered as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA, or operate through a Canadian-registered partner; (ii) unregistered foreign EMIs are prohibited from maintaining 'customer payment accounts' for Canadian-domiciled merchants; (iii) the CA_LP must not use an EMI as a pass-through for customer settlement funds because commingling would trigger a bank compliance rejection of the merchant's striped settlement reserves. Wise Business and Payoneer are acceptable as sub-rails for small-value foreign payouts, provided the principal treasury ledger remains at a Tier-1 Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec Limited Partnership, Canadian Schedule I banks generally require an in-person or live video-verified KYC interview with the authorized signatory of the General Partner (the individual or corporate entity with authority to bind the partnership) before activating cross-border disbursement services. Fully remote onboarding is permitted at the bank's discretion when the GP is a Canadian-incorporated corporation with verifiable directors, a valid Quebec NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec), and a federal Business Number (BN); in that case, electronic identity verification, corporate registry extracts, and a notarized signing-authority certificate may suffice. However, for a capital escrow account and for any account receiving non-resident limited-partner contributions, the majority of Tier-1 institutions will insist on at least one physical meeting at the branch or a bank-executive site visit. Non-resident limited partners who hold no signing authority are not required to appear; they must instead be disclosed through a current Schedule of Partners and a beneficial-ownership declaration, each attested by the General Partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Luxury resale product category with subjective valuation, authenticity risk, and potential invoice/consignment fraud surface; the bank perceives elevated typologies of money laundering through over/under-invoicing of high-value secondhand goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete chain-of-title file per high-value item: supplier agreement, authenticated certificates of authenticity from recognized houses (e.g., Sotheby's, Vestiaire Collective certification, Entrupy), independent appraisal certificate for items exceeding CAD 10,000, insured shipping waybills, and platform transaction/settlement reports from Stripe and Escrow_Pay demonstrating in-kind matching of inventory to proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited Partnership structure with passive non-resident Limited Partners concealing ultimate beneficial ownership; the bank cannot readily identify who controls the entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Attestation de société en commandite (Declaration of Limited Partnership) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, the underlying partnership agreement with exhibits, a formal Schedule of Partners listing every partner with a 25% or greater capital/profit allocation and their country of tax residence, tax identification numbers (Canadian BN/QST for resident; foreign TIN domestic for non-residents), a governance resolution confirming the General Partner's exclusive control, and an organizational chart prepared under FATF beneficial-ownership standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border funds flows between Canada, the United States, and European suppliers/buyers in the vintage luxury ecosystem create trade-based money-laundering (TBML) red flags around the pricing and authenticity of secondhand goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction trade dossier: commercial invoice indexed to the MT103 reference, customs entry evidence (CBSA import documents for goods entering Canada; ACE entry via US broker for exports), shipping tracking from DHL/FedEx/UPS, escrow release instructions matching shipping-confirmation events, and a monthly reconciliation statement certified by the GP linking each Escrow_Pay release to a corresponding inventory acquisition and sale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High velocity of small-dollar e-commerce settlements through Payment Service Providers (Stripe/PayPal/Escrow_Pay) viewed as potential smurfing/structuring through a merchant 'pass-through' account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PSP merchant agreements naming 'Quebec Limited Partnership' as the legal beneficiary, a do-not-commingle attestation from the GP, a documented cash-flow policy that all PSP settlements are swept daily to the Tier-1 bank operating account, and an independently prepared monthly reconciliation showing every settlement batch mapped to underlying order IDs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons (PEP) screening exceptions arising from non-resident limited partners or counterparties in jurisdictions associated with high-end goods transshipment (e.g., Russia-related, Chinese gray-market, or UAE-based intermediary traders).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written AML/ATF program evidencing automated screening against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), OFAC, and UN Security Council lists; a supplier/customer negative-media search report; contractual covenants from each vendor confirming origin of goods; and a board-level compliance certificate identifying all non-resident beneficial owners with over 25% interest in the CA_LP.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A non-resident investor wires capital to the CA_LP's Canadian operating or capital-escrow account via SWIFT MT103, or via a correspondent clearing arrangement (e.g., through the Canadian Payments Association's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) once credited to the Canadian bank). The MT103 field 50K must show the remitter/investor name exactly as due-diligenced; field 59 must show the beneficiary legal name of the CA_LP registered in Quebec (e.g., '[Partnership Name], société en commandite / Limited Partnership') plus its Canadian account number. The transfer's purpose message should state 'Capital contribution to Canadian limited partnership for e-commerce working capital.' No approval from the Bank of Canada is required. The Canadian receiving bank will (i) apply standard OFAC/CACR/SEMA sanctions screening, (ii) report the EFT to FINTRAC if at or above CAD 10,000, and (iii) request a supporting 'Capital Call Notice' signed by the General Partner describing the contribution amount, date, contributing partner, and the subscribed percentage, together with a GP resolution and a source-of-funds declaration for contributions exceeding CAD 100,000. Under the Investment Canada Act, the inbound equity contribution is not reviewable because the LP's enterprise value will remain below the 2025 WTO threshold (approximately CAD 1.851 billion for direct acquisition) and the online vintage-resale business is not a culturally sensitive activity. The bank will classify the inward remittance in its Statistics Canada balance-of-payments survey as Equity Capital of a direct investment enterprise (direct investment in Canada, equity) for statistical purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For acquiring vintage inventory from overseas suppliers (e.g., France, Switzerland, Japan, United Kingdom), the mandatory clearing mechanism is a corporate SWIFT MT103 message initiated from the bank's commercial online portal (e.g., RBC Express, BMO Mainstreet, CIBC Online for Business, National Bank's Command Center). Each MT103 must reference the underlying supplier invoice number and carry the beneficiary's IBAN; Canada imposes no FX-control approval step, but the bank may hold the payment for enhanced screening when the counterparty is an individual artisan dealer, requiring submission of a proforma invoice and proof of authenticity certification. For high-value inventory contracts above CAD 250,000, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit (MT700) confirmed by a Canadian Schedule I bank and governed by the UCP 600; the LC must be payable at sight with a required presentation of commercial invoice, authentication certificate, and transport document. For daily low-value settlement of e-commerce refunds and supplier micro-payouts, the CA_LP may embed Wise Business or Payoneer as a sub-rail, but those flows must reconcile monthly with the primary bank account. Where the LP holds a USD-dense settlement profile from Stripe/Escrow_Pay, it should maintain a dedicated USD float account at the Tier-1 Canadian bank and, optionally, a U.S. correspondent account (e.g., RBC Bank (Georgia) N.A. or BMO Harris N.A.) to eliminate double conversion on Canadian-dollar clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot CAD/USD outright FX transactions (T+0 or T+2 settlement) with the relationship bank.
Outright foreign exchange forward contracts in CAD/USD, EUR/CAD, GBP/CAD with tenors of 1–12 months (extendable to 24 months), documented under the Canadian Master Agreement or ISDA Master Agreement.
FX swaps and rollover swaps for temporary liquidity pivots between the CAD operating ledger and the USD float ledger.

Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) permitted only when aggregate non-CAD exposure exceeds CAD 10 million and the counterparty is a Schedule I bank with an approved trading line; documented under a 2002 ISDA Master Agreement.

Vanilla FX call/put options (CAD/USD, EUR/CAD) purchased from a Canadian bank under a negotiated ISDA/CSA credit support annex; no naked or speculative option writing without a separately approved trading limit.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are NOT permissible or necessary for CAD hedging in Canada because CAD is a fully convertible, CLS-settled currency with a deep onshore forward market; NDF quotes would be non-standard offshore exemptions and are not accepted by Canadian banking counterparties for resident-entity hedging.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating declaration for the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally during the annual filing period prescribed by the enterprise register, based on the partnership registration anniversary or applicable fiscal-year rule; verify the entity-specific deadline in the register portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing information may result in indexed administrative penalties, default notices, correction orders, and eventual cancellation of registration or administrative strike-off after continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update with the annual declaration and file prescribed changes promptly, generally within 30 days of a change in beneficial-owner information, subject to the applicable Quebec filing rule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or inaccurate information may trigger administrative penalties, correction requirements, prosecution exposure, and cancellation or loss of good standing in the enterprise register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally five months after the partnership fiscal year-end, where the partnership is required to file under the Income Tax Act and related administrative criteria.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may apply, including penalties based on the number of partners and the duration of the default; repeated non-compliance may increase audit, assessment, and information-demand risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership information return, Form TP-600-V
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally five months after the partnership fiscal year-end where a Quebec partnership information return is required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest may apply; Revenu Québec may issue compliance demands, assess partners using available information, and impose additional penalties for inaccurate or omitted information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST annual return, where annual filing frequency applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally three months after the fiscal year-end for a corporation, and four months after the fiscal year-end for other registrants, subject to the assigned reporting period and filing instructions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and arrears interest may apply; continued non-compliance can result in collection action, audit, assessment, and GST/HST registration or account restrictions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Quebec statutory independent-audit requirement or size-based audit threshold ordinarily applies solely because the entity is a limited partnership. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, financing documents, investor requirements, or a regulator.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting records must support Canadian tax and Quebec tax filings. Financial statements may generally use Canadian ASPE or IFRS where appropriate; IFRS is not automatically mandatory for a Quebec limited partnership.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A limited partnership has partnership interests rather than shares. Confirm the current general partners, limited partners, controlling persons, and ultimate beneficial owners annually; reconcile transfers and control changes against the partnership agreement and file required Quebec enterprise-register updates within the applicable statutory period.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of general partners and limited partners
Register of partnership-interest transfers and capital contributions
Register of beneficial owners and controlling persons
Minute book or formal record of material partner resolutions, where maintained under the partnership agreement
Accounting records, financial statements, tax returns, and supporting documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,200 annually for a Quebec registered office and local compliance or service address; Canada does not generally require a corporate registered agent equivalent for a Quebec limited partnership.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-10,000 for a voluntary review or audit of a small, low-complexity limited partnership; no audit fee is mandatory where no contractual or regulatory audit requirement applies.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%). The limited partnership is fiscally transparent; no entity-level tax is imposed on the LP itself. A corporate partner pays the combined rate on its allocable share of net business income; individual partners pay graduated personal rates (2024 top combined marginal rate in Quebec approx. 53.31%). Foreign partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP are subject to Part I tax on the Canadian-source business income attributable to the LP's Quebec permanent establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD): a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner may reduce the effective combined rate to approx. 12.2% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%). Quebec digital transformation tax credit (up to 30% of eligible expenditures, annual cap CAD 15,000); SR&ED refundable investment tax credits for eligible R&D in e-commerce logistics and authentication technologies; federal investment tax credit for clean-tech equipment; Quebec innovation tax credits for corporations in the retail-technology sector.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal) with T5013 Summary; filed electronically through CRA-certified software under the Partnership Internet File Transfer (PIFT) channel. Quebec accepts the T5013 data package under the Integrated Tax Administration Agreement (ITA Agreement), replacing the former provincial TP-600 filing for most partnerships; the LP must separately maintain its registration with Revenu Québec.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 Partnership Information Return due within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (December 31 year-end = May 31 of the following year). Partner T5013 slips must be distributed and filed with CRA by the last day of February following the calendar year in which the fiscal period ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the LP as registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, including the jurisdiction descriptor 'Quebec limited partnership'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name shown on the extra-provincial registration; a non-resident LP operating a Quebec establishment must register with Revenu Québec and CRA before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nine-digit CRA BN assigned to the partnership itself, distinct from the general partner's BN; the LP also requires a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident LPs must obtain a BN using Form RC460 (Request for a Business Number and Accounts) or through the CRA's Non-Resident Business registration desk before the filing deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of the LP's taxation year-end as defined in the partnership agreement and consistent with accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the fiscal period with the partner's own taxation year where possible to avoid stub-period allocations; any non-calendar year-end requires CRA approval under section 249.1 of the Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates the Canadian province to which the partnership is most closely connected; for a Quebec-established LP subject to management and control in Quebec, use Quebec (QC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The code drives the allocation of taxable income to Quebec for the provincial component of Part I tax; confirm the permanent establishment status of each non-resident partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total headcount of general and limited partners as at the fiscal period-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A T5013 return is mandatory if any partner is a non-resident, a corporation, a partnership, or if the LP has five or more members; transparency for each non-resident limited partner must be reported in the T5013 Summary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule of income and loss allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocates gross revenue, cost of goods sold (vintage luxury inventory), platform commissions, shipping, authentication, and administrative expenses to each partner in accordance with the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the limited partner 'at-risk' rules of subsection 96(2.1) to cap loss allocations at the partner's adjusted cost base; income allocations to non-resident partners are reported on T5013 slips and subject to Part I instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's allocable share of net business income from online consignment and secondhand luxury goods retail.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report this amount on their Canadian T2 or T1 return and may claim treaty-relief under the applicable business-profits article only if the income is not attributable to a permanent establishment in Canada; in most cross-border e-commerce structures a PE exists, so treaty business-profits relief is unavailable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 slip Box 10/12 - Foreign-source income and foreign taxes paid
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate reporting of income sourced to foreign jurisdictions (e.g. US marketplace sales) and foreign income taxes paid, enabling each partner to claim foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For US-source resale profits, file protective state income tax returns and claim the foreign tax credit on the Canadian return to avoid double taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013 filing: CAD 25 per day for each partner (up to a maximum of 100 partners and 5 months), subject to a minimum penalty of CAD 100 and a maximum aggregate penalty of CAD 2,500; false or incomplete information returns carry a per-slip penalty of CAD 100 (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 7,500) under subsection 162(5).
